To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a large proportion of the tables in our collection are similar in terms of table titles and header categories; (2) the header categories of tables that are related by their titles are often related to each other; and (3) the headers of related tables often have the same or related category names.
the Jaccard similarity of table title and header categories is a good measure for grouping tables from heterogeneous web sources.
the Jaccard distance can be used to cluster web tables with respect to their titles and header categories, and that this clustering can be used to reveal related content among heterogeneous tables.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of discovering the structure of a web table in terms of the fundamental indexing property.
the discovery and analysis of commonalities between the contents of web tables from diverse sources.
the automatic extraction of multi-dimensional views of web tables, and the use of these views to reveal related content across heterogeneous web tables.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we can cluster about one third of the web tables we examined into a dozen groups.
the Jaccard distance between the header sets of two tables is a reasonable indicator of the similarity between the two tables.
the Jaccard distance is a good indicator of the relatedness of web tables, and that this relatedness is often reflected in the titles and headers of those tables.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the table headers are more similar than the table contents.
the clustering results are promising, but that there is a lot of work to be done.
we have shown that there is a significant amount of related content that can be extracted from the web.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a simple and fast clustering algorithm can be applied to the headers of web tables to reveal related content among heterogeneous tables.
there are many commonalities between the tables from diverse sources.
, even for a relatively small collection of tables, there is enough commonality to be exploited for query formulation.
